title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.27301v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clinical AI evaluations are vulnerable to observation bias embedded in routine medical documentation, which captures only what clinicians notice, test, and record rather than a complete clinical picture. As this evidence travels into publications and reference knowledge graphs, crucial distinctions disappear: unexamined symptoms blur with confirmed negatives, and chronological disease progression is lost. Surviving evidence can also enter both the benchmark query and the reference knowledge base, creating a self-referential loop where a patient is evaluated against clues derived from their own published case report.   To quantify this bias, we tracked 6,503 clinical cases across six historical Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) releases (October 2021-June 2026) to identify when HPO first cited the publications describing them. translated_title: 观察到的、整理的、复用的：临床AI评估中的观察偏差
translated_abstract: 临床AI评估容易受到嵌入在常规医疗文档中的观察偏差的影响，这些文档仅记录临床医生注意到、检测和记录的内容，而非完整的临床图景。当这些证据进入出版物和参考知识图谱时，关键的区分便会消失：未经检查的症状与确认的阴性结果混为一谈，疾病的时间演变过程也会丢失。幸存的证据还可能同时进入基准查询和参考知识库，形成一种自我指涉的循环，即患者是根据从其自身已发表病例报告中提取的线索来进行评估的。为了量化这种偏差，我们追踪了6,503个临床病例在六个历史版本的人类表型本体（HPO）发布版本（2021年10月至2026年6月）中的情况，以确定HPO首次引用描述这些病例的出版物的时间。由此得到了一个具有可观察的“源摄入”事件的验证性队列，其中HPO引用了病例的源出版物……
tldr: 该研究揭示了临床AI评估中因医疗文档仅记录医生所见而产生的观察偏差，并通过追踪6,503个病例在HPO数据库六个历史版本中的引用记录首次量化了这一偏差，同时发现了证据同时进入基准与知识库所导致的自我指涉循环问题。
en_tdlr: This study reveals and quantifies observation bias in clinical AI evaluation—arising from medical documentation that captures only what clinicians observe—by tracking 6,503 cases across six historical HPO releases, and identifies a self-referential loop where patients are benchmarked against clues derived from their own published case reports.
